- .github/workflows/opencode-live-smoke.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 169-181 (the new `{ ... } >&2` diagnostic group inside `if [ "${call_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then`)
  Problem: The diagnostic commands (`opencode_strip_ansi < "${log_output}" | tail -n 120`, `cat "${clean_output}.jsonl"`, and `cat "${config_path}"`) run without any failure guard, while the step runs under `set -euo pipefail`. The immediately preceding `opencode_emit_failure_alert` call is deliberately guarded with `|| true`, but the new diagnostic block is not.
  Why it fails at runtime: `run_smoke_call` is consumed through process substitution (`IFS=$'\t' read -r ... < <(run_smoke_call ...)`). When the diagnostic block aborts the subshell, `read` receives EOF and returns non-zero; under `set -e` the whole live-smoke script then exits immediately. That truncates the run before the remaining configured model entries are exercised and before the final step-summary table and `exit 1` path run. A diagnostic failure, which should be best-effort, instead escalates into a truncated smoke run.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
